leaves.title: Projector Resolved Seed Calculus I
leaves.subtitle: Typed operator systems, seed rank, and exact packet coordinates
leaves.intro: Seeds, operators and projectors provide the linear language of the series. Exact packet coordinates make the generated objects and the maps between them visible.
leaves.scope: The correspondence concerns the stated proof-level constructions. Noncomputable existence results do not provide executable solvers.

leaves.title: Projector Resolved Seed Calculus II
leaves.subtitle: Refinement towers, weighted transfer, and integral separation of operator packets
leaves.intro: Refinement towers compare packet descriptions across levels. Weighted transfers and integral separation show which structures survive a change of resolution.
leaves.scope: Canonical values are defined for admissible data. A general existence theorem for admissible contours remains a separate question.

leaves.title: Projector Resolved Seed Calculus III
leaves.subtitle: Typed transfer, nonlinear packets, and obstruction theory
leaves.intro: Typed operations extend the linear language to nonlinear coordinates, analytic packet jets and obstruction theory. The analytic supplement develops the continuous packet-jet claims.
leaves.scope: Expanded ordinary proofs and the bounded Lean core have different coverage. The packet Taylor estimates, counting arguments and later extensions retain their stated ordinary-proof status. Arbitrary differentiability is not asserted.

entries.label: Analytic packet jets and exact composition

leaves.title: Projector Resolved Seed Calculus IV
leaves.subtitle: Cyclic analytic functions, reciprocal families, and spectral zero data
leaves.intro: A cyclic analytic family connects coefficient selection, differential transport, reciprocal polynomials and spectral zero data.
leaves.scope: The analytic statements retain their branch choices, multiplicities and integer-order hypotheses. Universal zero simplicity and a zeta functional equation remain outside these results.

leaves.title: Multiresolution Signal Calculus
leaves.subtitle: Exact coordinates, singular packets, and stable reconstruction
leaves.intro: Signal models move through filters, packet trees and reconstruction maps. Exact coordinates and singular packets distinguish representation from approximation and recovery.
leaves.scope: Separated-jump results require the stated model, gap and grid assumptions. Stable edge-packet recovery and the broader approximation class remain open.

leaves.title: Transfer Semigroups and Memory
leaves.subtitle: Probabilistic refinement, fractional operators, and exact hidden-state elimination
leaves.intro: Evolution, probability and conditioning share a transfer language. Eliminating hidden states produces memory terms whose hypotheses remain part of the model.
leaves.scope: Finite-state, common-gap and fixed-partition restrictions remain explicit. Completion, uniform refinement control and stable infinite latent-packet closure remain open. Floating residuals are not interval certificates.

leaves.title: Quantum Seeds and Effective Dynamics
leaves.subtitle: Symmetry, geometric transport, quantum channels, and bounded refinement towers
leaves.intro: Quantum seeds generate spaces through an operator grammar. Symmetry, circuits, geometric transport and quantum channels lead to finite effective dynamics and bounded refinement questions.
leaves.scope: The finite formal contract does not certify the full continuum physics program. Anomaly-free refinement, uniform Feshbach control, Lorentzian reconstruction and the proposed gravitational limits remain open.

leaves.title: Packet Operator Algorithms
leaves.subtitle: Exact compilation and GPU realization
leaves.intro: Structured packet representations remove work before execution. Exact compilation connects algebraic structure, recompression, precision and stated hardware observations.
leaves.scope: Small-core optimality uses supplied ordered thin-SVD equations and actual compact ranges. General numerical SVD verification, unrestricted discovery and CUDA-kernel verification require further results.

leaves.title: Euler Congruences
leaves.subtitle: Completion, factorial strengthening, and sharp dyadic geometry
leaves.intro: Euler congruences are developed through completion, factorial strengthening and dyadic geometry. The accompanying guides connect exact statements, bounded examples and formal coverage.
leaves.scope: The arithmetic, dyadic and lifting results have distinct hypotheses. General Euler-tail simplicity and the broader native and polyphase extensions remain open.

leaves.title: Universal Residual Seeds
leaves.subtitle: Deformation forests, transport categories, and conditional system completion
leaves.intro: Residual seeds, deformation forests and transport categories organize conditional system completion. Supplied arithmetic and carrier data remain explicit inputs.
leaves.scope: The target family and recovered carrier are independent existential outputs. Identifying them and proving nonzero occupancy require additional premises. Source families, carrier presentations and local comparisons remain supplied.

leaves.title: Tame and Wild Packet Geometry
leaves.subtitle: For local Langlands
leaves.intro: Tame and wild packet geometry organizes the local arithmetic constructions. The research companions retain both restricted progress and the unresolved obligations of Conjecture 66.
leaves.scope: Conjecture 66 remains open. Its unresolved requirements concern general arithmetic realization, H5 for the same candidate, corrected full-character occurrence and actual native data under the stronger contract.

leaves.title: Patching Support and Hecke Packets
leaves.subtitle: Conditional automorphic completion
leaves.intro: Patching support and compatible Hecke packets complete a conditional arithmetic argument. Each application must supply the geometric, automorphic and representation-theoretic inputs that the theorem uses.
leaves.scope: Actual residual and deformation data, applicable patching and full support, a compatible same-field Hecke point, classicality and an attached representation are required. Comparisons of compatible families assume those families already exist. Paper XI Conjecture 66 is not assumed proved.

leaves.title: Further studies in arithmetic realization
leaves.intro: These studies continue the questions of Chapter XI. Restricted constructions are presented with their hypotheses, while the remaining obligations of Conjecture 66 stay explicit.

leaves.intro: A further study of the arithmetic realization questions introduced in Chapter XI.

leaves.intro: These companions describe the formal sources, hypotheses and coverage associated with the twelve chapters. Read each formal statement with its declared inputs. The written mathematical arguments remain in the main sequence.
